chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed me on the authority of Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi, who said: Salama ibn Muhammad told me: Shaykh Al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) sent the Book of Adab to Qom and wrote to a group of jurists there, saying to them: Examine this book and see if there is anything in it that disagrees with you. They wrote to him that all of it is correct and there is nothing in it that disagrees, except his statement regarding the sa' in fitra: half a sa' of food, and the food for us is like barley, from each one a sa'.

key_terms.الصَّاع: Sa' (A traditional unit of volume measurement)
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra (Alms given at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: What is the juristic difference regarding the amount of fitra in Kitab al-Adab according to the scholars of Qom?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the scholarly rigor of the Qom jurists under the guidance of Shaykh al-Husayn ibn Ruh, who invited critical scrutiny to ensure the authenticity of 'Kitab al-Adab'. The jurists affirmed the text's general correctness but identified a specific fiqh discrepancy regarding the 'fitra' measurement, clarifying that the standard food is barley and the required amount is a full sa', contrasting with the half sa' mentioned in the book. This exchange exemplifies the Shia tradition of collaborative verification and precise legal derivation among the Four Scholars era.
